# Synthetic document-stack fixtures

These documents contain no customer data. They exercise the actual HTTP upload,
durable queue, worker, saved artifact, and download/rescan boundaries in
`scripts/verify_document_stack.ts`.

The gate also approves pending changes, reloads review decisions and checks
that the post-approval download retains the same bytes and scanner receipt.
See [the document journey guide](../../../docs/testing/document-review-journey.md)
for the coverage matrix, local stack and browser walkthrough.

- `course.pptx`: a title slide, "Course overview", with grey text on white.
  Expected deterministic contrast remediation: scanner score 92 to 100.
- `course.xlsx`: Course/Credits headings and one History/3 row. Expected
  deterministic workbook remediation: scanner score 49 to 100.
- `course.docx`: a level-two "Course overview" heading followed by eight-point
  "Tiny body text". The saved DOCX is a verified partial working file and remains
  downloadable. Manual findings remain in the unresolved totals; the file is not
  a complete accessibility result.

- `metadata.pdf`: generated by the existing `scripts/pdf_acceptance_corpus.py`
  metadata case. The full raw scan, rather than a filtered issue subset, produces
  a downloaded and rescanned artifact. The same measured checks and extracted
  text are retained; the missing PDF/UA declaration remains a manual finding.

- `simple_syllabus.pdf`: an existing synthetic PDF fixture. Remediation may
  deliver a partial working file while unresolved findings stay visible.
- `academic_paper.pdf`: an existing synthetic PDF fixture with checks the scanner
  cannot complete. It remains incomplete with no score; no working file or
  accessibility claim is inferred from the missing result.

A passing scanner score is not an accessibility conformance certification. PDF
semantic regression tests separately compare source and output checkpoint
results. Human review and write-back approval remain separate from a download.
